We've now walked the full journey and its rough edges. Here's where we stand — **10 behaviours are settled**:

1. **Effortless saving** — paste a link, its title, description, icon and preview are filled in for you, and you review/correct before it's saved.
2. **Your tags and note** — tag pills with suggestions from tags you've used, and a formatted note (with live preview) for why you saved it; all editable later.
3. **Search** — one box that finds across everything, with `#tag`, exact `"phrases"`, and `AND/OR/NOT (…)` logic, clickable tags, and honest highlighting.
4. **To read vs Finished** — your library opens on *All*, with focused views and status chosen when saving or editing.
5. **Archive** (reversible, tucked aside) and **Delete** (permanent, confirmed) — clearly different.
6. **No duplicates** — re-saving a link takes you to the existing one to edit it instead.
7. **A gentle first-run welcome**, and honest handling when a page can't be read.
8. **Readable long content** and friendly empty states.
9. **Large libraries** load as you scroll, with search/filter/count/sort always spanning the whole collection.
10. **Sorting** — five orders, a remembered default, applied everywhere.

I've also noted, for later, a couple of quality items (a concrete speed target for big libraries; staying usable on a phone) and one idea beyond this round (flagging dead links) — none of which block us.

I believe we've explored the goal thoroughly and your recent reactions are refining wording rather than changing behaviour. **So I'd like to switch from exploring to actually building this — implementing exactly the scope of the ten behaviours above as the real, running application. May I start building it?**

(Once you approve, my role changes from facilitator to implementer — I won't start until you say so.)
